describes: Thin roofing slate in courses, the sveitser house's roof: a dark blue-grey that weathers a little lighter and duller.

value.describes: The slate's own lightness, CIE L* of its visible reflectance (D65, the 1931 2° observer), new and old: it goes from one to the other over oldYears, as srgb does. The street's clay and colour take it (blender/parts/street/paint.json deposit.values); the page's moss, lichen and eave grime are marks over it.

source.newL: Measured rock, not a roof: grey phyllite, ECOSTRESS Ward85, Y 0.126, L* 42.2, C* 2.8; Norway's roofing slates are phyllites, quartzites and mica schists (https://snl.no/skifertak). Beside it a fresh grey slate, ECOSTRESS Ward92 (Pen Argyl, Pennsylvania), L* 37.0. No source names Stavanger's quarry.
source.oldL: Measured: a weathered slate roofing shingle off a government building, grey, ECOSTRESS 0680UUUSTO, spectrum integrated with D65 and the 1931 2° observer: Y 0.172, L* 48.5, C* 2.7 (https://speclib.jpl.nasa.gov/ecospeclibdata/manmade.roofingmaterial.shingle.solid.all.0680uuusto.jhu.becknic.spectrum.txt); its age and city are not given. Dirt draws a dark surface lighter and greyer (Sleiman et al. 2011).

notes.relaidYears: How many years a slate roof lies before it is stripped and relaid on new battens and nails, its good slates reused, each keeping relaidKeeps of the weathering it had.
notes.laid: How the slates are laid (English pattern, rectangular slates about 250 by 500 mm, each course breaking joint by half a slate): the slate's width, the course's length up the slope (the gauge), how far a course's foot stands proud (the slate's thickness, pushed a little so the butts hold as a line at the street stop), the joint between slates, and each slate's own seeded roll about the slope and drop at its butt (mass-made slates hung by hand: non-semantic texture, claiming no history). The ridge is a low capping; at the verge the slates stop against the barge board, which stands above them.
notes.srgb: Screen colours judged by look; not the town's own slaty rock (slate.json), which is a wall and step stone.
notes.water: Its water profile as the town's (Shaders/Water.hlsl, Overstory.World.WaterPack): how much it darkens wet, how glossy its wet film, how long it holds water, how readily run-off stains it. Slate sheds water and glazes, as the town's slate. Judged by look.
